title: How to Get Stains Out of Fabric Car Seats: Blot, Don't Scrub
meta_description: Get stains out of fabric car seats by blotting, not scrubbing, and using as little liquid as you can. What to use, what to avoid, and when it needs extraction.
excerpt: Most seat stains go wrong in the first five minutes: rubbing spreads them and soaking drives them into the foam. Here's what works at home, stain by stain, and what shampoo and extraction does when DIY runs out.

faq.q: What is the best way to get a stain out of a fabric car seat?
faq.a: Blot it with a clean white cloth rather than rubbing, then use a small amount of upholstery cleaner made for car interiors, worked from the outside of the stain inwards. Rinse by blotting with a damp cloth and dry the seat quickly.

faq.q: Why is there a ring on my car seat after cleaning it?
faq.a: That's a water mark. The water spreads outwards through the fabric and leaves dirt behind at the edge as it dries. Use less water, and clean the whole panel out to its seams so it dries evenly.

faq.q: Can I use household cleaners on car seats?
faq.a: It's safer not to. Bleach and strong household products can lighten the fabric or leave a sticky residue, so use a cleaner made for car upholstery and test it on a hidden area first. Never mix products.

faq.q: Can every stain be removed from a fabric car seat?
faq.a: No. Shampoo and extraction remove most stains, but ink and dye can bond with the fibres, and fading, burns and wear are damage rather than dirt. Send us photos in daylight and we'll tell you honestly what's likely to come out.
